title: The Workflow supervises a run and stops orchestrating it
description:
The Run Workflow's job shrinks to what docs/design/cloud-factory.md always said: 'boot the orchestrator sandbox, watch it, enforce wall-clock and cost budgets, retry a dead orchestrator, finalize'. It does not plan, dispatch, collect, gate or close.

Shape, all verified against Cloudflare's docs:
- boot the container with keepAlive: true, which heartbeats every 30s and prevents idle shutdown (it does NOT defeat host-restart eviction; nothing does), and destroy() in a finally - a container under keepAlive 'must be explicitly destroyed... to prevent containers running indefinitely and counting toward your account limits'.
- step.waitForEvent for the orchestrator's completion, with a timeout. Waiting instances 'do not consume concurrency slots'; the timeout is settable from 1 second to 365 days and THROWS on expiry, which is the re-boot-and-resume path.
- on timeout: git fetch and LOOK before concluding anything. The branch is the source of truth; the event is an optimisation that avoids polling.

Also fix the two defaults that bit us: a step inherits timeout '10 minutes' AND retries { limit: 5, delay: 10000, backoff: exponential }. The retry default is the dangerous one - a timed-out step re-ran the whole pass and re-dispatched model work up to five times, which is very likely what exhausted the GitHub hourly budget (uim). Any step that can start paid work needs a deliberate retry policy, not the default.

When this lands, q35's slot heartbeat becomes scaffolding for a shape we have left: remove it and let the TTL stand unassisted. Keep eg9's reporting - a refused release should still name who holds it.
acceptance_criteria: The Workflow only boots, budgets, watches, retries and finalizes; no step that can start paid work carries the default retry policy; a container is always destroyed; and a timeout re-boots into resume rather than concluding failure
